title: A passkey campaign switched on by Microsoft
lede: A first-seen service principal created a credential policy and edited another inside one second. Both writes trace to a Microsoft-managed change to the tenant's registration campaign. No person initiated anything.

verdict.customer_action: Confirm the passkey registration campaign was intended; if not, move it off "Microsoft managed" in Entra.
verdict.text: Microsoft's managed setting retargeted MFA registration from Authenticator to FIDO2. No containment required; expect a tenant-wide wave of passkey enrolments.
verdict.impact: None to any account. The change is a Microsoft-managed setting; every user will be asked to register a passkey, and no credential was weakened or removed.

respond.headline: Confirm with the customer
respond.note: If they did not want enforced passkey registration, move the campaign off Microsoft managed.

grounds.title: Three reasons it looked bad, tested
grounds.intro: No AI-assist verdict was attached; these are the grounds the summaries themselves raise.

items.claim: An unknown service principal wrote an authentication policy.
items.finding: `00000000…` is **Azure Credential Configuration Endpoint Service**, a Microsoft first-party service. It wrote routine MFA-method updates for users all month — 9/1, 9/9, 9/21 — in `Office365`.

It is the backing object for a registration-campaign change written **0.3 s later** in `AzureAuditLogs` by **Microsoft Managed Policy Manager**: target `microsoftAuthenticator` → `Fido2`, snooze 1 → **0**, `Policy.Features` 0 → 16.

items.claim: First time this key or behavior has been seen.
items.finding: The base rate is **1 in 30 days** for any entity on either rule — the shape of a one-off tenant-level rollout, not a campaign of intrusions.

timeline.title: The sequence, from the audit log
timeline.intro: The summaries say 19:40:00. That is the two-minute bucket label; the events below are the raw times.

rows.event: Update policy — **Default Policy**, no properties changed
Authentication Methods Policy Update — campaign target → `Fido2`, all users

items.title: No human policy change.
items.body: Zero user-initiated authentication-policy writes in 30 days; every policy write came from Microsoft-managed identities.

items.title: No methods removed.
items.body: Subsequent writes by the same principal carry empty property diffs.

response.intro: What to do next, and what has already been done. Nobody had to act before this review.
response.todo_intro: Nothing to contain. One conversation with the customer closes it.

done.text: The registration campaign was retargeted from Authenticator to FIDO2 by **Microsoft Managed Policy Manager**; the two policy writes followed within a second.
All three grounds were tested against the audit log. Every policy write came from a Microsoft-managed identity; no person initiated anything.
Nothing was contained. **None was required**: no method was removed and no credential was weakened.

recommendation.label: Close · benign
recommendation.text: Close benign. Brief analysts that forced passkey registration will fire the AzureAD add-authentication-method rules across the user base; treat that wave as one campaign.

recommendation.label: Confirm · with the customer
recommendation.text: Tell the customer the change was Microsoft-managed. If they do not want enforced passkey registration yet, move the registration campaign off “Microsoft managed” in Entra.
